A follow-up to [this post](<https://mlcollyer.github.io/collyerblog/posts/2026-10-15-How-RRPP-evolves/>)

# Where we left off...

The `getLSmeans` function, used within `pairwise` was updated to have better memoization. Let's see how it works now, after we install the updated version.

```{r, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
pak::pkg_install("mlcollyer/RRPP")
```

## Data Example

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(geomorph)

# make a latticed cube
vert <- 8
template <- expand.grid(1:vert, 1:vert, 1:vert)
colnames(template) <- c("x", "y", "z")

# Groups
ng <- 10
nw <- 10
group <- factor(rep(1:ng, each = nw))
n <- length(group)

# add points for n specimens

LMlist <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(.){
  as.matrix(template + rnorm(length(template),
                   mean = 0, sd = 0.3))
})

```

### GPA

```{r}
LMa <- simplify2array(LMlist)
GPA <- gpagen(LMa, print.progress = FALSE)
plot(GPA)
```

## RRPP

```{r}
Y <- two.d.array(GPA$coords)
dim(Y)

system.time(
  {fit1 <- lm.rrpp(Y ~ group, 
                 iter = 999,
                 Parallel = 1,
                 turbo = TRUE);
  AOV1 <- anova(fit1)}
)
AOV1
```

## And now for the moment of truth!

```{r}
system.time(PW <- pairwise(fit1, 
                           groups = group))

system.time(S1 <- summary(PW))
S1
```

## An improvement of about 2 seconds!

This might not seem profound but it is worth remembering that the `pairwise` function is doing more than calculating means. For example, it is also calculating group variances.

```{r}
system.time(S2 <- summary(PW, test.type = "var"))
S2
```

And vector correlations...

```{r}
system.time(S3 <- summary(PW, test.type = "VC"))
S3
```

And standardized vector distances...

```{r}
system.time(S4 <- summary(PW, test.type = "stdist"))
S4
```

The reason these take practically no time to summarize is because they were all calculated with the initial `pairwise` use. This is why `pairwise` will always take longer than `lm.rrpp`, but as this example shows, it does not mean computational slogs need to be accepted.
